claims.text: Pre-coating W particles with a thin, vapor-deposited Cu layer before consolidation will improve W–Cu interfacial bonding.
Pre-coating W particles with vapor-deposited Cu will reduce void formation in the consolidated composite.
Pre-coating W particles with vapor-deposited Cu will enhance thermal transport under irradiation relative to conventional fabrication methods.
Conventionally sintered or powder-infiltrated W–Cu materials often suffer from interface defects and phase separation.
Vapor deposition can produce a conformal Cu coating on W particles.
A uniform Cu interfacial layer minimizes voids and discontinuities.
A uniform Cu interfacial layer promotes continuous bonding between W and the Cu matrix.
Vapor deposition ensures near-perfect, defect-free Cu coverage of W particles.
Uniform Cu coating enhances wetting during subsequent W–Cu processing.
Uniform Cu coating enhances diffusion bonding during subsequent W–Cu processing.
Enhanced wetting and diffusion bonding minimize phase separation and void formation.
The resulting microstructure preserves thermal properties under fusion-joint service conditions.
The resulting microstructure preserves mechanical properties under fusion-joint service conditions.
Cu-pre-coated W–Cu will have lower interfacial defect density than material made by spark-plasma sintering or mechanical alloying without pre-coating.
Cu-pre-coated W–Cu will have higher thermal conductivity than material made by spark-plasma sintering or mechanical alloying without pre-coating.
Cu-pre-coated W–Cu will have greater mechanical durability under irradiation than material made by spark-plasma sintering or mechanical alloying without pre-coating.
Spark-plasma sintering, mechanical alloying, and Cu infiltration into a W skeleton often leave interfacial voids.
Phase separation in conventionally fabricated W–Cu impairs thermal transport.
The proposed intervention is applicable to fusion-reactor joints exposed to high temperatures, irradiation, and thermal cycling.
The long-term stability of the vapor-deposited Cu coating under combined thermal cycling and irradiation is not established.
